key_insight: ReImagine learns high-fidelity human appearance via image generation first, then uses that learned appearance as a strong prior for video synthesis, decoupling appearance modeling from motion and camera dynamics to achieve controllable, high-quality human videos.
problem_solved: Addresses the difficulty of jointly modeling human appearance, motion, and camera viewpoint under limited multi-view data, which previously forced trade-offs between controllability and visual quality.
method: Train an image-first appearance model to capture detailed, multi-view-consistent human appearance as a reusable prior.
Condition a separate temporal synthesis module on the learned appearance prior plus motion and camera controls to produce coherent videos without degrading appearance quality.
Use controllable inputs (e.g., skeletal poses, camera parameters) and multi-view/temporal losses to enforce consistency and enable fine-grained control.
impact: Enables practitioners to generate controllable, photoreal human videos with higher visual fidelity even when multi-view data is limited, improving workflows in animation, virtual production, and downstream video editing.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: 'Image-first appearance training' → 'Appearance prior' → 'Temporal video synthesis with motion & camera controls'.
Before/after frames comparing joint-training methods vs. image-first approach (showing improved appearance fidelity).
Control illustration: input skeletons/camera parameters mapped to generated video frames to show controllability.
Architecture block diagram highlighting the appearance prior module and separate temporal module with loss/regulatory signals.
paper_title: ReImagine: Rethinking Controllable High-Quality Human Video Generation via Image-First Synthesis
paper_authors: Zhengwentai Sun, Keru Zheng, Chenghong Li, Hongjie Liao, Xihe Yang
